- **Needs the new game:** the server choice on the start card (the line "Choose the server you fly from" and the "Could not check the servers" toast are in 13 languages), the server row on a pilot's name card, the sidebar, the rail, the Launch button in the header of every page and the tour card; the new Dungeon words (the door line, the plan-wide count, the three booster kinds, the lobby count, the ring on the Warlord's ship); the drawings of the new rockets (the gravity well, the Support pulse, the puff of Flares, the rings under the status rockets); the new wiki and Help texts.
- **Server only, live with the server:** the rockets' stats, prices, recipes and cooldowns, the launchers, the rocks' hit points, pay and ore, the pay of the eight rock-breaking missions, the Pirate Boss's rocket, the Auction's rocket lots, every Dungeon number, the mission hull limits and the Global chat relay.

**For administrators and the server**
- **Clan Dungeons: no new table, column, route, setting or data step.** The only data that moved is `server/Resources/Dungeons.json` (written by `docs/design/dungeons-model.py --json`, never by hand), so `GET /api/admin/dungeons` shows a new `file.hash`. The file is read at the start and checked whole: a file that is there and wrong stops the start with nothing changed. `python -X utf8 docs/design/dungeons-model.py --check` was green on the Dungeons v2 lane's branch (run 2026-11-09; not run again on this note's branch).
- **The file and the code belong together.** A 0.5.2 server does not know the door rule `eliteShare`: given the 0.5.3 `Dungeons.json` it fails to read the file and the start is stopped. A 0.5.3 server with the 0.5.2 file runs no boosters. A rollback brings the 0.5.2 image together with its own file. Server and game go live together (stage both, flip together).
- **First days, the counters** (`GET /api/admin/counters?prefix=dungeon`; the healthy values are expectations from the rules and the model, not seen on a live server): `dungeon_boost_window{stage}` up to ten a run and none at stage 1, about 8 for a party that opens the door and flies on; `dungeon_boost_picked{kind,auto}` has five kinds; `dungeon_door_opened{door=boss, why=kills}` at 75 % of the elites; `why=admin` stays rare. The admin overview's `boosts` object of an active run has new keys, `{kills, earned, windows, of, open, answered, picks: {damage, hull, shield, speed, recharge}}`.
- **The Dark Matter model:** the dungeons now give more than the Dark Matter model's single source (a clan of five that runs the three stages every day gets 74 to 222 Dark Matter a day before, twice that now). Read the Dark Matter stock of the first days against the excavators' burn.
- **Global chat between the servers: nothing to set up** (the node uses its `NODE_SECRET`; a Home with no node registered behaves as before). Look at it with `GET /health`, `flight.chat` (`relay`, `ringHead`, `ringLen`, and per node `pushAgeMs`, `pullAgeMs`, `pushed`, `pulled`, `dropped`). Home's log has every Global line as `CHAT: [global] [<node>/<World>] name: text`, and the speaker's own server logs it as well.
- **Chat kill switch, no restart:** `PUT /api/admin/flight/dials` with `{"chat": {"relay": false}}`; each server then keeps its own Global. The dials replace each other as a whole (a PUT without `asteroids` lifts the asteroid dials, one without `chat` turns the relay on), and they live in memory, so Home's restart is the default (on). A `chat.relay` that is not a JSON boolean is a `400 BAD_DIALS`.
- **Chat: two things nobody has looked at on the real boxes** (`docs/DEPLOY.md`, "Global chat between the servers (0.5.3)"): whether Sliplane's edge holds a request for 8 seconds (a cut is taken as an empty answer, so chat still works), and which address Home sees for each node (it decides what is counted per address).
- **Missions:** a server rule (`quest::world_hull_limit`, `world_hull_pct`); no data step.
- **`GET /api/servers` with a token costs one account read on every request,** a 304 included, because the list differs for administrators. At the station that is about one primary-key read per signed-in pilot per minute, and one per 5 seconds while the start card or the Launch dialog is open. A cheap fix is known (cache the admin flag per user for a short window) and is not done; this is a client release.
- **Proof of the tour card:** `tour::tests_settle`, `tour::tests_flicker` and `tour::tests_card` hold each cause; several of the flicker tests failed on 0.5.2's code when they were written (not run again for this note).

releases.lead: SpaceCorps 2027 0.5.2 rebalances the ships: every base ship has new hull, speed and laser numbers, the thirteen designs follow their ships, every ship has an auxiliary slot, the Helios Beam hits softer, and three design abilities are stronger (Venom, Heal Pod, Blink). The Wraith gets a tenth hull plate slot with a technology of its own. The Clan Gates become Clan Dungeons, and their boss room opens when 75 % of the aliens are destroyed. It adds keys and screens that are easier to learn (Esc closes windows, a shorter sidebar), a skippable tour for new pilots, Auction lots for each world, and the first build of flying from other servers, which stays switched off until it is opened.

**If you already play: what changes for you**
- **The numbers are the server's.** Ship hulls, speeds, slots, the Helios Beam and the abilities reach every game at once, with the server. A 0.5.1 game shows them (it reads the server's numbers) but its help cards and design descriptions keep the old words until you update the game.

- **A 0.5.1 game keeps working with the 0.5.2 server.** The old game still says "gate" in its own windows until you update, shows the server's new dungeon messages in English only, and counts the room's "left" as the kills still needed, so its objective line is right for the new rule except for the word "guards".

- **Your board is your world's.** The Lots page shows the lots of the world you fly in when you open it. If you choose another world after a wipe, you see that world's lots.
- **A lot you lead stays with you.** In the rare case that your world changes while you lead a lot (a world is chosen at Setup and again for the next season, and the wipe voids the open lots and refunds the leading bids), the lot stays on your list with a small world capsule, you are refunded at once if you are outbid, and you get the goods when it ends. The "In bids" capsule counts the lots you lead in every world, and your results show the lots you won in any world.

The worlds' own lots begin with the next UTC hour; an hour that 0.5.1 already made lots for is left as it is.
- **The Market is as it was.** Listings and buy orders reach pilots of all three worlds, and the Market's prices are not split.
- **Smaller lots in a thin world.** In a world with few active pilots the lots are small (down to a tenth of the table); in a busy one they are full size. In the model's run with 17 pilots who look at the Auction, split 10 / 4 / 3 across the worlds, the goods on offer in total hardly change (151.6 M against 152.7 M a day). How many pilots look at the Auction in each world today is not measured.

Pick another row in the Launch sheet to fly from it; the game remembers the pick for that pilot on that PC until you pick another. - **This part moves nothing.** The server list and the flights add no data step and touch no pilot row; no Credits, Thulium or items move because of them, and no pilot changes anything until they pick another server. (The release's own data step `hulls-v3`, which scales the saved hull of some ships, is separate and not part of this lane.)

**Flying from other servers (built, switched off)**
- **Choose where to fly: a server list (needs the new game).** The game can list Helsinki (the server it plays on today) with **Singapore** and **US East**. A row shows the name and region (Europe, Asia, North America), a ping the game measures itself, the pilots in flight there and a status (Open, Updating, Down, Full, Maintenance, Staff only; "Update the game" when the server speaks a newer version of the flight protocol than the game, "Being updated" when it speaks an older one). The ping is a TCP connection to the server's port 443, three tries, the smallest, read again every 20 seconds while the list is shown: green under 80 ms, amber from 80 up to 150, red above 150. The list is on the start card under the server line and in the Launch sheet, where you pick the row to launch from. The pick is remembered for each pilot on that PC. A pilot who never picked, and one whose picked server is full, down or of another version, launches from Helsinki. A launch that is refused gives a message and leaves you at the station.
- **Off at release: you see nothing new.** When 0.5.2 goes live no regional server is registered, so the list holds Helsinki alone. The game then draws no list and offers no choice: the start card and the Launch sheet look as in 0.5.1 and every flight is flown from Helsinki. Singapore and US East appear only after the owner has set them up (see the administrators' part), and they stay "Staff only", listed and launchable by admin accounts alone, until he makes them public in a separate step. That step is not part of the release.
- **The same pilot on every server.** Helsinki keeps the pilot: account, ships, items, Credits, Thulium, clan, rank and the station. When you launch on Singapore or US East, Helsinki lends that server a copy of your flight data for the flight, under one exclusive lease (one flight per pilot, on one server at a time). The regional server reports to Helsinki every 30 seconds and at the dock; Helsinki applies each report once, so a repeated or late report is never counted twice. What the flight earns (Credits, Thulium, experience, honor, kills, loot, the ammunition used, hull and position) is applied to the same pilot in Helsinki, and level and ranking points are worked out there from the merged figures. If a regional host and its disk are lost, at most the last 30 seconds of one flight's rewards are lost; a host that restarts with its disk sends what the disk holds when it is back.
- **A flight, start to finish.** "Connecting to Singapore…", then the flight with a "Flying from Singapore" badge at the top right. Return to Base shows "Syncing your flight to the station…" (the game gives the respawn and the last settings save up to 3 seconds, then the server waits up to 5 seconds for Helsinki to confirm), then the station with the rewards. If Helsinki has not confirmed, the sheet reads "Waiting for the station to receive your flight…" for up to 30 seconds; after that you are at the station and told "Your flight's rewards are on their way to the station.", and the station shows them when Helsinki has them. A flight that ends without a dock (the server was told to send flights home, you launched elsewhere, or the server lost its link to Helsinki and ended the flight) ends with "Your flight from Singapore has ended. You are back at the station."; a server that refuses your connection says "Singapore did not accept your connection. You are back at the station."
- **The station stays in Helsinki.** A regional server only flies. Shop, Assembly, Skylab, Auction, clan actions, bonus codes, Hangar edits, mission claims, accounts and payments are refused there (the server answers "Available at the Station: dock to use it.", in English): dock (the dock waits up to 5 seconds for Helsinki to confirm), use the station, launch again. A regional server does take respawn, swapping the ship configuration, your settings, accepting, tracking and cancelling missions, and the reads a flight needs (Hangar, inventory, abilities, research, profiles, the map, the online list). While your ship is away Helsinki refuses your station actions too ("Your ship is on a flight from another server. Dock first."). How each in-flight window shows the station-only refusal was not checked one by one.
- **What does not count while you fly on a regional server.** These are switched off there, in code: achievements, the Logbook, the clan line, the Wardens and the Clan Dungeons, containers and special items, the news feed, the Auction, Invite Friends and the login calendar. Davidski's kills pay nothing there (the kill feed tells the pilots he has paid out for the day). Rank, crown and ranking points are Helsinki's: a regional server has no ladder, and Helsinki's ladders move after it has applied the flight.
- **Each server is its own sky.** Its pilots, aliens, swarms, excavators, bosses, chat, groups and PvP are its own and are not shared; you meet only the pilots flying there, and there is no chat or group across servers. Each regional server has its own Alpha, Beta and Gamma, and your world choice travels with you. The season day, the Peace Protocol and the wipe countdown are Helsinki's and reach the regional server with every beat (every 5 seconds).
- **One flight at a time, and the newest launch wins.** Launching on another server, or at Helsinki, while a flight is away brings the first flight home first: its final report is applied before the new flight is granted (3.0 seconds in the proof, at most about 8). The older game is told its flight has ended.
- **Season wipe.** No new flight is granted from five minutes before the wipe (the list reads Maintenance and the row's tip says a season wipe is about to start; no countdown is drawn). Flights go on until about 30 seconds before the wipe, when every flight on a regional server is sent home with its rewards. A regional server takes flights again after it has rebuilt its worlds for the new season and told Helsinki (in the proof about 10 seconds after the countdown ended).
- **Your sign-in stays in Helsinki.** The game gives a regional server only a launch ticket that is valid for one minute and works once, never your token or password. The regional server makes its own token, which Helsinki does not accept, and Helsinki's token is useless there. The game sends a ticket only to an https address that ends in `.sliplane.app` or `.spacecorps.xyz` and that the list from Helsinki named.
- **The aim, and what is measured.** The aim is a shorter round trip in flight for pilots far from Helsinki; the station stays in Helsinki, so its menus are as far away as before. Measured from a PC in the Helsinki area (a home line) to the real Sliplane boxes: 182 ms to Singapore and 96 ms to US East (a WebSocket echo). **Not measured:** the round trip from a pilot's home to Singapore or US East, so no figure is promised. Each regional server takes 60 flights at a time.
- **Texts.** The list, the sheets, the badge, the messages for a flight that ended and the refusals of a launch and of Helsinki's "Dock first" line are in all 13 languages. The refusal of a station action on a regional server arrives as the server's English sentence.

- **Metric route.** `POST /api/player/tutorial {"step", "outcome"}`, signed in, answers `204`. `outcome` is one of `reached`, `done`, `skipped` (Skip this step), `stuck` (the skip button appeared), `left` (the consent skip of the whole tour), `replayed`; anything else is `400`. `step` is one of the 28 ids (`m01` to `m11`, `f01` to `f17`, listed in `docs/design/onboarding-steps.golden`) or `tour`; anything else is counted as `other`. **60 calls a minute per pilot** (`429` above), a body of at most **512 bytes** (`413` above). - **Metric `fun.tutorial{outcome, step}`** is a daily counter (group `fun`, entry in `docs/design/admin-metrics-catalog.json`), aggregate only: no pilot id, no name, no table, so no privacy-page change. Read it as: reached against done against stuck against left per step; the completion rate is `tour/done` over `tour/reached`; `left` is recorded under the step the pilot was on, so the consent skip rate is all `left` events over `welcome` (`m01`) reached. There is no Tutorial card on the Admin Funnel page yet. The existing `fun.quests`, `eco.burned`, `ret.rate` and `acq.signups` are the before-and-after comparison.
- **First start of 0.5.2 for this part:** no data step, no migration, no environment variable, no wipe change. Three additive settings keys appear in pilots' `settingsJson` as the new game writes them: `tutorial` (versioned, `v` 1; a value of a future version is left untouched; the game writes `running`, `done` and `skipped` and never `pending`), `sidebarMore` and `keyBindingsMigrated`. The docs say the web client ignores keys it does not know; that was not tried for `tutorial`.
- **Starter kit.** `STARTER_AMP` = "Damage Amp I" is granted at the first enlistment only, with `Origin::Starter` (never marketable). If the seeds had no such item the kit would skip it.
- **Known limits.** (a) The lane's docs record no run by a person who has not seen the game; the tour was driven by the scripted pointer on a scratch server, and the minutes above are sums of nominal seconds. (b) Dialogs that draw raw egui buttons (not the kit's) take no chord and wear no caps; the connection-lost card does not answer Enter (Retry is a click); Esc on the Landing page is as it was. (c) A binding saved as Shift+Esc is not reserved, and the ladder takes an Esc whatever modifier it carries, so such a binding would fire and close a window in the same press. (d) The wiki's Getting Started keyboard table still lists Esc only for denying an invitation, and the wiki's Spacemap Travel page still calls the Galaxy Map the "Star System" window. (e) A window under 1280 points wide has no Windows guide.

releases.lead: SpaceCorps 2027 0.5.1 reworks the Clan Gates: the maze is the whole map under fog, the party starts together from a shut room, the Warlord's room stays locked until the elite aliens are dead, and a clan portal, a call card and a window of its own bring the clan to the gate, and the gates open from season day 1 (day 4 in 0.5.0). It opens Beta and Gamma to swarms, giant excavators, Danger Sector rocks and PvP from season day 1, starts the ranking of this season from zero, keeps what is fitted in your Skylab at a wipe, and pays a mission by the higher of the world it was done in and the world you fly in. It also makes the Boss Crystalys twice as tough, gives the Tesseract 100 Facets, takes the Power Cores out of the ammo crafts, lets the excavator keep its Excavator Mining buff, joins the item stacks the Transport Cache split, and fixes the Steam link.
releases.whats_new:
**Highlights**
- **Clan Gates, reworked (needs the new game).** The maze fills the whole map (20 by 11 cells) and the flight view has fog. The party waits in a shut start room and the run begins by itself when everyone has arrived. The Warlord's room is locked until the **Crystalys and their Twins** are dead (45 of 235 aliens for a party of 5), packs you wake hunt you through the corridors, and the Warlord has **seven abilities** and a laser that hits about twice as hard.
- **Getting to the gate (needs the new game).** A **Clan Gate portal** on your company's home map, a **call card with Join** while your clan's gate waits for pilots (Settings > General > Groups > **Clan gate alerts** turns it off), and the gate's bar is a **Clan dungeon window** you can drag, close with its red light and open again from a new toolbar button.
- **Clan Gates open from season day 1** (day 4 in 0.5.0), in every world. The wipe disbands every clan, so on day 1 your clan is new: found it, bring **4** pilots of the level the stage asks for (**6 / 7 / 8**) and put the price into the clan bank (**500,000 Credits** for stage 1). The clan bank's own reward still asks for a clan **3 days** old with 3 paid pilots, so the clears of days 1 to 3 pay the pilots and not the bank; the caps are the same (**3 gates a day**, **10 paid clears a week**).
- **More room to play.** Time limits **95 / 130 / 165 minutes** (80 / 110 / 150). **Six** loot zones (four), a zone is held up to **three times faster** with five pilots in it (**10 seconds**), and from stage 2 on you choose a **booster** three times a run.
- **Pay.** Every paid pilot also gets **5 / 10 / 15 Orvium Reinforced Plates**, and a **gear card** (14 pieces, stage 3 only, 1 % of the cards) now gives **every paid pilot a piece forged for him**, not one copy to one pilot: each pilot rolls his own enchant tier (most come out Standard, a higher tier up to Eternal is a rare find).
- **Beta and Gamma start on day 1** (server; the new game shows it right). In Beta and Gamma the **swarms**, the **giant excavators** and the **Danger Sectors' asteroids** are there from **season day 1**, and **PvP is on from day 1**: the Peace Protocol of the first three days is Alpha's alone. Alpha is as it was: PvP, swarms and Danger Sector asteroids from day 4, excavators from day 11. The Dormant Swamp and the rest of Tech Surge stay on day 11 in every world.
- **The ranking starts from zero for this season** (server). The wipe of 6 November was meant to start a fresh ranking and did not: the Hall of Fame, the ladders, your rank and the crown still showed the points of the season before. From this update they count only what you have earned since that wipe (00:05 UTC on 6 November); the kills you made before it no longer count towards your rank, and the explanation in the game and the wiki say so in all 13 languages. The **all-time board** (lifetime PvE points) is not affected, and nothing is taken from you: no Credits, Thulium, items, level, experience, honor or kills move. A kill made since the wipe is counted in full.
- **Items you have equipped in your Skylab stay at a wipe** (server). The engines and lasers fitted in the Engine and Defense Modules, with their thrusters and amps, are kept where they are, still fitted. The Help card and the Cache page say so in the new game.
- **A mission pays the higher of the world it was done in and the world you fly in** (server). The wipe let you choose your world again but left the missions you had done or begun alone, and they were still paid the world of the season before. Now the hand-in pays the higher of the two: done in Alpha and handed in from Beta, a mission pays 2x; from Gamma, 3x. You can hold a hand-in until the update is live.
- **Boss Crystalys is twice as tough:** hull, shield and volley doubled, the pay unchanged, **30** PvE points a kill (21).
- **The Tesseract fights with 100 Facets** (50), 20 at a time (10), at speed **750** (450). They fly all round it and fire at the nearest pilot who has hit it. Its plates are now **a private box for every pilot the kill pays**, half the amounts.
- **Ammo crafts without Power Cores or Ship Fragments.** Ultra Core, Experimental Fusion Core and Dark Matter Ammo I are made from Cataclysite and Quorvium.
- **Excavator Mining stays with the excavator.** The share of the pilot who starts it is the excavator's until it rests, and every box it lays carries it.
- **Item stacks split by the Transport Cache are merged again:** the same resource, ammo or rocket that showed as three to five tiles with different counts is one stack with the sum, and the wipe keeps it that way. Nothing is lost or moved: only the rows of one item are joined (what is in your cache, fitted or on a ship stays as it is).
- **Magic Hammer:** the limit of one in 60 days is gone.
- **The Steam link works again** (server fix: no game update needed).
- **Windows on a software renderer** (a virtual machine with no graphics card) no longer crashes at the start (needs the new game).

**If you already play: what changes for you**
- **Update the game.** The server and the new game go live together. The update itself pays, moves and removes no Credits, Thulium or items (the one change to what you hold is that the stacks of one item that the Transport Cache split are joined; every unit stays).
- **A 0.5.0 game keeps working** but cannot open or enter a Gate: it is told "Update the game to open or enter the new Gates." What is marked (server) below reaches a 0.5.0 game too.
- **A Gate that is open when the server updates ends** with the restart, as for any restart; its price goes back to the clan bank.
- **Your ranking points start from zero for this season.** When the new server starts, the Hall of Fame, the ladders, your rank and the crown show what you have earned since the wipe of 6 November (a pilot who has made no kill since it reads 0 until his next one). Your level, experience, honor, all-time kills and the all-time board stay as they are.
- **Missions waiting for their hand-in, or still running from before the wipe:** you can hold them until the update is live and hand them in then. A mission pays the higher of the world it was done in and the world you fly in when you hand it in, so one you did in Alpha before the wipe pays 2x from Beta and 3x from Gamma. Choose your world first.
- **Your Skylab:** nothing to do. At the next wipe the engines and lasers fitted in its modules stay fitted.
- **Pilots of Beta and Gamma: PvP, the swarms and the Danger Sectors' rocks are on from the first day.** If the season is on day 1 to 3 when the server updates, they begin at the restart (the swarms and the rocks within a second, the excavators at once); nothing is wiped and no pilot is moved. The next wipe starts them on day 1.
- **Pilots of Alpha notice no change in when the swarms, the rocks, PvP and the excavators start:** the Peace Protocol still holds days 1 to 3, and the swarms, the rocks and PvP come on day 4, the excavators on day 11. Only the Clan Gates open earlier, on day 1, in Alpha too.
- **A 0.5.0 game in Beta or Gamma** is fought for and fights as the server says (the ship's PvP badge, a refused or allowed shot and the enemy markers come from the server), but its Dashboard, Season and Gates pages still show the **Peace protocol** (and no PvP mark) on days 1 to 3, because they read the one flag of Alpha. The new game shows the pilot's own world.

**What needs the new game, and what does not**
- **Needs the new game:** everything in the Clan Gates (a 0.5.0 game cannot open or enter one; the new maze and its fog, the start room, the boss room's notices, the boosters, the portal, the call card, the window and their texts and sounds), the 30 PvE points in the Help card and on the Rankings page, the Help card's lines about the ranking that starts from zero at every wipe, about the Skylab's fitted items and about the day PvP opens in each world, the Cache page's line about them, the Dashboard, Season and Gates pages' tip for the Peace Protocol in the pilot's own world, the swarm and rock missions' briefs (day 1 in Beta and Gamma), the excavator sheet's lines about the buff, and the Windows start-up guard.
- **Server only, live with the server (a 0.5.0 game gets it):** the Boss Crystalys numbers and pay, the Tesseract's 100 Facets and plates, the three ammo recipes, the excavator's buff on every box and its start message, the Magic Hammer without a limit, the ranking that starts from zero for this season, the Skylab's fitted engines and lasers kept at a wipe, the world a mission pays, the item stacks the Transport Cache split (joined again), everything in "Beta and Gamma from day 1" (a 0.5.0 game only shows the Peace protocol wrongly on three pages, see above), and the Steam link fix.

**Clan Gates, reworked**
- **How a run goes.** On the **Gates** tab a co-leader or the leader picks a stage and presses **Summon**; the price comes out of the clan bank, as before. Clan members cross with **Enter** or through the clan's portal (below) while they fly, in a group with at least **4** members of the clan. Everyone lands in the **start room**, whose door is shut. When you enter, the gate starts waiting for the members of your group who are online and not away; **the run starts by itself when all of them are inside and at least 4 pilots are**, or when the room is full (10). The pilot who opened the gate or an officer can still press **Start** at once with whoever is inside, if at least 4 pilots are. The start room's door opens with the run. A gate nobody starts within **10 minutes** closes and its price goes back to the bank.
- **When it opens.** **Season day 1**, the first day of the season, in Alpha, Beta and Gamma alike (0.5.0: day 4, with the swarms). The gates need neither the swarms nor PvP, so the Peace Protocol days are no reason to wait. A gate costs Credits from the clan bank, not Gate Parts. A server that updates in the middle of a season just reads the new day at its start: nothing is stored with the old one.
- **The maze is the whole map.** One of **8 layouts** on one of 6 maps (Gate Delta, Epsilon, Zeta, Eta, Theta and Iota): 20 by 11 cells, corridors 720 units wide, a **start room** at the west edge, **six loot rooms** and the **boss room** at the east edge, each with one door. Walls stop ships and shots. **Fog:** the flight view draws walls and aliens only in the rooms and corridors you have explored and within 2,400 units of a ship of your party; your party's pilots are never hidden. The minimap keeps drawing only the explored rooms.
- **The aliens.** Four kinds sleep in the corridors: Gate Goombah, Gate Pirate, Gate Crystalys and Gate Crystalys Twin, **235** for a party of 5 (195), the same at every stage, at most 10 alive for each pilot and 70 in all. A pack wakes when you come within 6 cells, and **a pack you wake hunts you** through up to 16 cells of corridor. About a tenth of the packs (7 of 71 for a party of 5) already stand in the corridors when the run begins, idle, and go for a pilot who comes within 4 cells. Stage 2 aliens have **1.5 times** the hull, shield and damage of stage 1, stage 3 **2 times**. The Crystalys and the Twins take back 0.01 % of the damage their volleys do.
- **Every alien stands inside the maze.** A pack comes on the map in its cell, its members round the **middle** of the cell, never behind a wall: that holds for the packs of the plan, a loot zone's wave of 12 Goombahs and a Crystalys, the Goombahs of the Warlord's **Swarm assist** and the packs that stand in the corridors from the first tick. (In 0.5.0 a wave or a Swarm assist could put a Goombah on the far side of the outer wall, where no pilot could hurt it, and a wave counts as cleared only when every alien of it is dead.)
- **The boss room is locked.** It is shut from the summon, and **the Warlord inside cannot be hurt** (a lock on it is refused with "The target cannot be hurt right now."). It opens when every **Gate Crystalys and Gate Crystalys Twin** of the run is dead, 45 of the 235 for a party of 5; the window's objective line says "Destroy the guards to unlock the boss room (N left)". Once open it stays open. The Warlord is shown when you come to its room. It never leaves its room, the door shut or open: a pilot in the corridor can draw it only to the room's edge, and through an open door it still fires at whatever its laser reaches.
- **Loot zones.** Each maze has **6**, one in each loot room. Stand in one for 2 seconds and a wave of **12 Gate Goombahs and a Gate Crystalys** (10 and 1) comes for it. Hold the ring: it takes **30 seconds** with one pilot in it and runs **1.5 / 2 / 2.5 / 3 times as fast with 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 or more pilots** in it, so it takes **10 seconds with five**; the hold stops while 3 or more aliens stand in the ring. Then the group has 45 seconds to vote for one of three cards. A card is Thulium (2,000 / 3,000 / 5,000), Velkonite Reinforced Plates, Velkonite or Orvium ore, Ultra Core, Experimental Fusion Core, Dark Matter or a Dark Matter Plate, and now and then (**1 %** of the cards, **stage 3 only**) a piece of gear: Starfire-III, Helios Beam, Engine III, Adaptive Core III, Heavy Shield Core, Momentum Thruster IV, Impulse Thruster IV, Hull Plating II or III, Damage Amp IV, Crit Amp IV, Penetration Amp IV, Capacity Shield Cell IV or Absorption Shield Cell IV. The Orvium Reinforced Plates are no card any more: they come with the pay (below).
- **Boosters (stages 2 and 3).** After the 2nd, 4th and 6th wave of the zones is cleared a window opens for **30 seconds** and every pilot chooses **Damage, HP or Speed**: **+1.5 %** a pick at stage 2 and **+3 %** at stage 3, at most 4.5 % and 9 % of one kind. Damage is your lasers' (rockets do not use it) and HP is the ship's maximum hull. A pilot who does not answer gets HP. Leaving the gate, or being destroyed in it, takes your boosters off your ship, and they come back when you fly back into the same gate; they end for good when the gate is cleared or ends, and nothing is saved. Stage 1 has none.
- **The Warlord.** A Crystalys three times the size, with **10,000,000 hull and 8,000,000 shield** at stage 1 for a party of 5 (15 and 12 million at stage 2, 25 and 20 million at stage 3), tougher with every pilot in the party. Its laser hits for a whole number between **12,500 and 15,000** at stage 1, **15,000 and 17,500** at stage 2 and **20,000 and 25,000** at stage 3, a new number every volley. It uses one ability at a time, at random, each with a cooldown of 2 minutes (3 for the Swarm assist). **Seven abilities:**
  - **Lifesteal aura** and **Shield absorption:** as in 0.5.0.
  - **Meteor drop:** the meteors land with an explosion and a damage number, and the warning rings appear at once.
  - **Rocket barrage:** it now fires only at pilots the Warlord has a clear line to, and a red mark follows the pilot a rocket is after (an EMP Charge or a cloak still shakes the rockets off).
  - **Focus Most Wanted** (it was Focus on healers): for 20 seconds the pilot who has dealt the most damage to the Warlord wears a gold bracket that everyone sees, and the Warlord fires an extra bolt at him every second for 1.5 times a volley. Before anyone has dealt damage it is not used.
  - **Swarm assist:** the Warlord calls **12 / 18 / 24 Goombahs** (stage 1 / 2 / 3, for a party of 5, more for a larger party). Until they are dead, or 60 seconds, it cannot be hurt and does not shoot.
  - **Zone of Chaos:** a violet ring of radius 900 round the place where the Warlord stands when it casts it (the ring stays there), a 2-second warning, then 15 seconds in which **pilots inside it cannot fire** (lasers, rockets, Venom and Focus Fire). Pilots outside can fire into it, healing, cloaking and moving still work, and the Warlord's aliens fire as usual. A pilot who tries hears "You can't attack inside the Zone of Chaos."
- **Time.** A gate fails and pays nothing after **95 / 130 / 165 minutes** from its start (80 / 110 / 150), or when nobody has been inside for 3 minutes. After the Warlord falls the gate stays open for 2 more minutes. A pilot who left or was destroyed can fly back in **3 times, 20 seconds apart**. **Calculated, not played:** a whole run for a party of 5 should take about **41 / 66 / 74 minutes**.

| Stage | Pilot level | Price | Aliens, hull / shield / damage | Warlord, hull + shield for 5 | Time limit | A run for 5 (calculated) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6 | 500,000 Credits | x1 | 10 M + 8 M | 95 min | about 41 min |
| 2 | 7 | 1,000,000 Credits | x1.5 | 15 M + 12 M | 130 min | about 66 min |
| 3 | 8 | 2,000,000 Credits | x2 | 25 M + 20 M | 165 min | about 74 min |

- **Getting to the gate.**
  - **The clan portal.** From the summon until the gate ends, a **Clan Gate** portal stands on each company's home map (M-1, T-1 and G-1). Only your clan sees it. Fly up to it and jump as at any other portal (the **J** key, a 3-second charge) and you enter the gate by the same rules as **Enter**: a ship in flight, out of combat, at the stage's level, in a group with at least 4 clan members.
  - **The call card.** While your clan's gate waits for pilots, the clan's pilots who are flying elsewhere get a card at the top of the screen with **Join** (the Gates tab's Enter) and **Not now**, and a sound. A pilot whose group mate has already gone in is told so: the card comes back, even after Not now, and says his group is waiting for him. The pilot who opened the gate is not called (unless a group mate of his has gone in), a docked pilot is not told, a pilot below the stage's level is not called, and no pilot is called for the first time in the last 20 seconds of the wait. A clan is called for at most six gates a day. The card does not form the group: it says what is missing. **Settings > General > Groups > Clan gate alerts** turns it off.
  - **The Clan dungeon window.** The gate's bar (the stage, the clocks, the objective, your party's hull bars, the zone hold bar, **Leave**) and the Warlord's ability banner are one window now: drag it by its title bar, close it with its red light, open it again with the new **Clan dungeon** button of the toolbar (it is there while you are in a gate). It opens by itself once for each gate you enter; one you shut stays shut for the rest of that run. While it is shut and the Warlord's ability works, a one-line strip shows it and a click on the strip opens the window.

**Pay**

| Stage | Honor | Experience | Credits | Thulium | x4 ammo | Orvium Reinforced Plates | Clan bank, first clear |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 25,000 | 600,000 | 5,000,000 | 4,000 | 4,000 | 5 | 10,000,000 |
| 2 | 50,000 | 1,500,000 | 10,000,000 | 9,000 | 9,000 | 10 | 20,000,000 |
| 3 | 100,000 | 2,400,000 | 17,500,000 | 15,000 | 15,000 | 15 | 30,000,000 |

- **Unchanged from 0.5.0:** the Warlord's fall pays, not the aliens; a stage pays a pilot **once per UTC day** and a pilot is paid for **10 stage clears a week** at most; a clan opens at most **3 gates a day**; a clear without a share in the fight (2 % of the Warlord's hull and shield, or 10 of the gate's aliens, or 50,000 healed during the fight, and 2 minutes inside) pays nothing and the result screen says why; no world multiplier; the experience counts for PvE ranking points; the clan bank gets its Credits the first time the clan clears a stage in a season.
- **New:** the plates come with the pay, **5 / 10 / 15 for every paid pilot**, in place of the plate card of the vote. **A gear card gives every paid pilot of the party a piece forged for him** (his own roll of the Assembly's odds), not one copy to one pilot; a pilot who is not paid gets no card either. The gear cards are 14 pieces (four in 0.5.0) and **stage 3 only**: stages 1 and 2, which could offer gear in 0.5.0, offer none now. The result screen names the tier a piece was forged to (for example Godly Starfire-III).
- **What a day and a week can bring a pilot:** every stage once in a day pays 175,000 Honor, 4,500,000 experience, 32,500,000 Credits, 28,000 Thulium, 28,000 x4 ammo and 30 plates; the best week (seven stage 3 and three stage 2 clears) pays 850,000 Honor, 21,300,000 experience, 152,500,000 Credits, 132,000 Thulium, 132,000 x4 ammo and 135 plates.

**Beta and Gamma from day 1**
- **What each world has, by season day.** Alpha: days 1 to 3 the Peace Protocol (nobody can attack a pilot), the swarms, the Danger Sectors' asteroids and PvP from day 4, the giant excavators from day 11. Beta and Gamma: the swarms, the excavators, the Danger Sectors' asteroids and PvP from **day 1**. The Dormant Swamp, the Dormant Swarm's move to it and Tech Surge's other changes begin on day 11 in every world; on that day Beta and Gamma are told only that the swamp stirs (their excavators already stand), Alpha is told the whole of event 2.
- **A server that starts in the middle of a season** (a deploy on day 2 or 3) builds all of it at the first tick, with no wipe: the swarms, the standing excavators and the asteroid fields of Beta and Gamma are there within seconds, Alpha's wait for their days.
- **The next wipe** starts Beta and Gamma on day 1 with new swarms, the excavators standing and the fields full.
- **Where pilots may fight is as before:** Beta everywhere but its base sectors `x-1`, Gamma everywhere outside safe zones, Alpha in `x-4` and the Danger Sectors. What changes is the day.
- **Warning: the Danger Sectors' rocks are the richest in the game.** A Motherlode pays **348,900 to 581,400 Credits and 165 to 381 Thulium** at the base rate, **twice** that in Beta and **three times** in Gamma; the Rich Lodes, Prism Clusters, Ancient Husks and Star Crystals around it are the next best. They are on from the first day in Beta and Gamma, in the sectors where pilots fight, and the missions that ask for them (levels 7 and 8) open with them. Watch Credits and Thulium of Beta and Gamma in the first days after the wipe.
- **What protects a pilot who arrives there after the wipe.** A pilot lands at the gate of the home sector `x-1` of his company at about (1000 ± 200, 1000 ± 200), inside the **station's safe zone** (radius 1,600 round (1500, 1500)), where nothing can be hurt; **Beta forbids PvP in every `x-1`**, so the base sector is free of it for the whole season; in **Gamma PvP is allowed everywhere outside the safe zones**, so a pilot who leaves the ring can be shot from the first day. A ship that has just respawned after a destruction is **calm for 3 seconds** (it cannot be hurt or fire). Nothing else protects a pilot in Gamma, and none of this is new.
- **The Peace Protocol of Alpha is unchanged,** and a 0.5.0 game cannot show the other worlds' days (see above).
- **For the game** (needs the new game for the display only): `GET /api/wipe/timeline` keeps `pvpEnabled` (Alpha's, for 0.5.0 games) and adds `pvpFromDay {Alpha, Beta, Gamma}`; the Dashboard, the Season page and the Gates strip read the pilot's own world's day, and the season bar has no red mark where there is no Peace Protocol.

**The ranking of this season**
- **It counts from the wipe of 6 November** (server). That wipe (00:05 UTC) started season 2, and the Hall of Fame, the ladders, the ranks and the crown went on showing the points of the whole career, because the setting that makes a season's ranking start from zero said season 3. It says season 2 now. When the new server starts it counts every pilot's PvE and PvP points again from the figures it took at that wipe, and clears the rank each pilot was told and the pay that repeated PvP kills had given up. It does this once; a second start changes nothing, and the points you earn after the first start are never cleared.
- **What does not move:** Credits, Thulium, items, level, experience, honor, the totals of your kills, the **all-time board** (lifetime PvE points) and the final ranking of the season that ended, which is still in the season history. The update pays nothing and takes nothing back.
- **From now on** the points start from zero at every wipe, as the Rankings explanation in the Help card says (13 languages); the wiki pages Ranks, Seasons and Rewards and Wipe Timeline say the same.

**The Skylab at a wipe**
- **What is fitted stays** (server). At a wipe, the engines in the Engine Module and the lasers in the Defense Module stay fitted where they are, in the same module and slot, with the thrusters and amps fitted into them. They take no place in the Transport Cache and no weight of its cargo.
- **What goes as before:** the Trophies Bay's loot (it is emptied), and a piece you have taken out of its module, which is a loose item like any other.
- **In the game** (new game): the Help card's "What survives the wipe" and the Cache page's keep line say so, and the Cache page's summary of what is kept counts the fitted items. For administrators: `GET /api/admin/wipe/preview` has `items.skylabFitted`.

**Missions from an earlier wipe**
- **A mission pays the higher of the world it was done in and the world you fly in when you hand it in** (server). The wipe let you choose your world again but left your missions alone, so a mission you had finished and not handed in, or one you had begun, was still paid the world of the season before: **1x for everyone who played Alpha and now flies Beta or Gamma.** Now the hand-in pays the higher of the two: the credits, Thulium, experience and honor are **2x in Beta and 3x in Gamma** (the items and the booster time are the same in every world), a mission you did in a higher world than the one you fly in keeps the higher multiplier, and a mission you began in a higher world and finish in a lower one counts as done in the lower one.
- **Nothing is changed in your account.** The rule is read at the hand-in: the update pays nothing by itself and no pilot has to hand a mission in before it. **You can hold a hand-in until the update is live.** A hand-in made before it is paid as it is today.
- **Inside one season nothing moves:** a pilot cannot change his world between two wipes (an administrator can place him), so a mission begun and handed in in the same season pays the world it was done in, as before.
- **The Admin page** shows the world a waiting hand-in pays now (`world` of `GET /api/admin/players/<id>/quests`).

**Boss Crystalys**
- **Twice as tough** (server). The leader of the Crystalys swarm in `DS-1` to `DS-3` has **twice the hull, twice the shield and twice the volley**; its guards, its pay and its box are as they were.

| Boss Crystalys | Alpha | Beta | Gamma |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hull | 896,000 | 1,344,000 | 1,792,000 |
| Shield | 560,000 | 840,000 | 1,120,000 |
| Laser, a volley a second | 10,000 | 15,000 | 20,000 |

- **A larger group.** Calculated, in Alpha: six level 8 pilots in Paragons with x2 ammo can bring it down if its fire is spread over them, nine if it is all on one pilot; with x4 ammo five and six. A pilot alone is destroyed.
- **PvE points.** A kill is worth **30** (21). The server counts every pilot's points again when it starts, so the Boss Crystalys you killed before count 30 each; nobody loses points.

**The Tesseract**
- **100 Facets, 20 at a time** (server). While the Tesseract is hit, **20 more Facets** come every 5 seconds, up to **100** (10 and 50). A Facet flies at speed **750** in every world (450). A Facet has the same hull, shield and volley as before (20,000 hull, 16,000 shield, 556 a volley in Alpha), pays nothing and adds no PvE points.
- **A skirmish, not a chase.** The Facets no longer hunt the pilot with the most damage. Each flies short legs of its own to random places in a ring of 1,800 units round the Tesseract and fires at **the nearest pilot who has hit the Tesseract** that is within its range. A pilot who has not hit it is never their target, and a pilot who keeps beyond the ring and the range of a Facet's laser is not shot at. When nobody is left in their reach they leave 25 seconds after the last hit.
- **Plates for everyone the kill pays.** The three plates (Reinforced Hull Plate 1 to 2, Velkonite Reinforced Plate 3 to 6, Orvium Reinforced Plate 1 to 2, with the same chances, about half of the 0.5.0 amounts) are no longer in the top dealer's box. Every pilot the kill pays gets a **private box** of them that only he can see and take, for 10 minutes, rolled for his share of the damage as a Clan Warden's loot is; in a group each pilot gets his part of the group's share. The top dealer's box keeps the Power Cores, Ancient Control Units and, now and then, Dark Matter.

**Laser ammo crafts**
- **No Power Core and no Ship Fragment** (server). The three crafts that asked for them now ask for Cataclysite and Quorvium, the two commons the aliens drop, and a little more Thulium. A batch is still 1,000 units made in the Assembly; the ammo you hold and the research you made stay as they are. Per 1,000:

| Ammo | 0.5.0 | 0.5.1 |
|---|---|---|
| Ultra Core | 1,000 Cataclysite, 1,000 Ship Fragment, 100 Power Core, 4 Velkonite Reinforced Plate, 500 Thulium, 360 Credits | **1,200 Cataclysite, 900 Quorvium**, 4 Velkonite Reinforced Plate, **568 Thulium**, 360 Credits |
| Experimental Fusion Core | 1,000 Cataclysite, 1,000 Ship Fragment, 100 Power Core, 1,000 Quorvium, 8 Velkonite Reinforced Plate, 1 Orvium Reinforced Plate, 1,050 Thulium, 9,138 Credits | **1,400 Cataclysite, 1,050 Quorvium**, 8 Velkonite Reinforced Plate, 1 Orvium Reinforced Plate, **1,176 Thulium**, 9,138 Credits |
| Dark Matter Ammo I | 2,000 Cataclysite, 2,000 Ship Fragment, 1 Dark Matter, 800 Thulium, 4,913 Credits | **1,200 Cataclysite, 900 Quorvium**, 1 Dark Matter, **868 Thulium**, 4,913 Credits |

- **What did not move.** The model keeps what a unit is worth (200, 440 and 245 Credits), so no price in the Market, at Davidski or at the Auction changes. The Skylab Ammo Printer, the other four ammo crafts and every research are as they were.

**Excavator Mining**
- **The buff is the excavator's** (server). The pilot who presses **Start mining** with the Pilot research Excavator Mining gives the giant excavator his share, **+20 / 30 / 40 %** in all, and the excavator **keeps it from run to run until it rests** (the buff goes when the rest after an overheat or a destruction is over, or when an administrator resets the excavator). **Every box it lays holds that much more,** Thulium and ore alike, whoever pressed Start, fuelled it, switched the resource or picks the boxes up. Before, the share was the run's and the next Start replaced it, so a researcher who only fuelled, or who started after a pilot with no research, saw the base amount.
- **Who changes it.** A later Start by a pilot with a higher level raises the buff and he becomes its giver. A Start with the same or a lower level, with no research, or by an administrator never lowers it. A run that ends when the fuel runs out keeps the buff. An excavator that is running when the server updates goes on, and the share of the pilot who started it becomes its buff.
- **The sheet** (new game) shows the buff, the pilot who gave it and whose run it is in every state, and tells a pilot with the research whether his Start would give or raise it; the start message names the share the excavator carries.

**Item stacks**
- **Why you saw the same item many times.** When you put loot in the Transport Cache, every trip left one more stack of the same item, and the wipe turned each cached stack into a loose one beside your own. The Auction sells whole lots out of one stack, so a stack of 34 Daraxium or 2 Nyxite (lots of 100) could never be listed and the stacks could not be combined.
- **What 0.5.1 does** (server): the first start of the server joins the stacks of every pilot: for each item the oldest stack gets the units of the others, and the Auction tag keeps counting the units that could be listed (a stack of 100 listable units and 50 Shop units is 150 units with 100 listable). The wipe now does the same for every pilot after the cache is reset, so it cannot happen again. Your units, your cache, your Skylab's fittings and what is on your ships do not change; an item with another enchant is never joined with a plain one.
- **What stays:** the units that do not fill a lot (for instance the last 34 of a lot of 100) still cannot be listed, but once for each item instead of once for each stack.

**The Magic Hammer**
- **No limit of one in 60 days** (server). A Hammer can be given again at once; a pilot still holds at most 5. A bonus code line can give up to 5 Hammers (1 before). Nothing gives Hammers out by itself: an administrator or a bonus code does, and a Hammer is still never in a container.

**The Steam link**
- **"Link Steam Account" works again** (server). In 0.5.0 it always ended with "Steam did not accept the ticket". Valve refuses a check code of 32 or more characters, and the server's was 32; it is **30** now (found on a real Steam client, which accepted 30 and 31 and refused 32 and more). The released game needs no update. **Not yet tried:** a complete link on the live server with the new code.

**Windows on a software renderer**
- **No crash at the start** (new game). A Windows PC that draws with Microsoft's software renderer (WARP) could close the game a few seconds after the start, before the first picture, because of a fault inside a Windows component. It was seen on GitHub's Windows test machines (virtual machines with no graphics card); Windows Sandbox and a Windows without a graphics driver use the same renderer but were not tried. The game now notices a processor-only Direct3D 12 adapter and does its culling on the processor, with no compute shaders. On those machines the 0.5.0 game started 0 to 2 times of 8; the login screen now started **8 of 8 times**, headless and in a window. A PC with a working graphics driver does not pick the software renderer.

**For administrators and the server**
- **The first start of 0.5.1** does four things, in this order, and writes each in the log: the data step `fresh-season-v1` (once; the ranking of the running season starts from zero, see "The ranking of this season"), the recount of every pilot's PvE and PvP points from the baselines of the 6 November wipe, the data step `stack-merge-v1` (once; it joins the stacks the Transport Cache split, one log line for each pilot changed and one summary line that ends `0 pilots refused`; every pilot in a transaction of his own, units and Auction labels checked before and after, a pilot whose totals would change is rolled back and the step runs again at the next start), and, in a season that is on day 1 to 3, the swarms, the standing excavators and the Danger Sector rocks of Beta and Gamma at the first tick. Nothing is written for the missions' world rule or the Skylab's fitted items: both are read at the moment they matter (a hand-in, a wipe). DEPLOY.md, "First start of 0.5.1", lists the log lines to look for. `FRESH_SEASON_V1_DRY_RUN=1` and `STACK_MERGE_V1_DRY_RUN=1` on a copy of the volume run the data step, roll it back, log what it would do and exit.
- **Worlds' days:** `GET /api/wipe/timeline` keeps `pvpEnabled` (Alpha's, so that a 0.5.0 game keeps working) and adds `pvpFromDay {Alpha, Beta, Gamma}`. `POST /api/admin/asteroids/gate {world, enabled, payPercent, supplyPercent}` turns a world's rocks off or lowers their pay at once, with no restart.
- **Missions:** `GET /api/admin/players/<id>/quests` shows the world a waiting hand-in pays now (`world`).
- **Item stacks:** `POST /api/admin/players/<id>/inventory/merge` joins one pilot's split stacks at once (audited, answers what it merged; the first start and every wipe do it for all pilots). DEPLOY.md, "Item stacks merged (0.5.1)", lists the log lines.
- **Unlock:** `POST /api/admin/dungeons/runs/<runId>/unlock {note}` opens the boss room of an active run whatever is left to kill, for a run that cannot be finished. It writes a `dungeon-unlock` record, and a second call changes nothing. A force-clear of a run whose boss room is still shut pays like any clear and its record says so.
- **Counters:** `GET /api/admin/counters?prefix=dungeon` gains `dungeon_boost_window`, `dungeon_boost_picked`, `dungeon_ability_hit`, `dungeon_door_opened{door=start|boss}`, `dungeon_call_sent`, `dungeon_call_joined` and `dungeon_call_skipped`. DEPLOY.md, "Clan dungeons 0.5.1", says what healthy looks like.
- **The Dungeons tab of the admin page** shows, for each run, whether its boss room is locked and how many guards are left, how many of the pilots the start room waits for are inside, and the boosters picked; it has an **Unlock boss room** button (a note is asked for) and its force-clear sheet lists the Orvium plates and the gear pieces (the tier of a piece is rolled when it is paid).
- **Client feature `gates-2`:** the routes that summon, enter and use the portal answer 426 to a game that does not announce it.
- **Hammer codes:** the Codes tab shows no "once in 60 days" hint and a line may give up to 5 Hammers; the administrator's `force` flag stays for a file that asks for a window.
- **Excavator:** the administrator's reset takes the buff with it.
- **Release job:** it can hold before the deploy until it is told to go, so that the server and the game flip together; its test limit is 240 minutes, and the dungeon model's check (`docs/design/dungeons-model.py --check`) is a step of its checks. `SPACECORPS_DRAW_PATH=cpu|indirect|multi|count` forces the game's draw path for diagnosis.

releases.lead: SpaceCorps 2027 0.5.0 is the PvE update: clans open Gates, mazes with a Warlord at their end, three boss swarms and the Tesseract mothership roam the sectors, and laser ammo gets a research tree. Every alien fires its own shots, a wipe reopens your missions for their full pay, and shield cores, Engines, Field Theory and the Afterburner are retuned.
releases.whats_new:
**Highlights**
- **Clan Gates.** From season day 4 a co-leader or the leader opens a Gate from the clan bank (**500,000 to 2,000,000 Credits**); **4 to 10 clan members** cross a maze, hold **4 loot zones** and bring down the **Warlord**. Stage 3 pays each pilot **100,000 Honor, 17,500,000 Credits, 15,000 Thulium and 15,000 x4 ammo**, once a day and **10 paid clears a week** at most. It is the **Gates** tab of the clan window, and it needs the new game.
- **The Tesseract.** A mothership in Danger Sector 4 with **1,600,000 hull and 1,200,000 shield** in Alpha. It mends **125,000 a second** when left alone and calls **up to 50 Facets** while it is hit. A fight for a very large group.
- **Three boss swarms.** A Boss Phantasm and a Boss Goombah on `x-3` and `x-4`, a Boss Crystalys in `DS-1` to `DS-3`, each with guards that heal it.
- **Laser ammo research.** **Military Grade Ammo I and II** open the crafting of x3 and x4, and **the x4 is no longer sold**. New: **Siphon Battery II**, **Antimatter Battery I and II** (they pierce **20 %**) and **Dark Matter Ammo I and II** (**x1.5 to x5** a volley; **x6** with a shield leech). The Pirate Boss drops Siphon Battery II.
- **Every alien has its own shot** and its own sound: blobs, spores, shards, slugs, ion orbs and slag, with **32 new sounds**. Your lasers are unchanged.
- **After a wipe your missions come back.** Every mission you completed, the 50 Challenge missions too, opens for one **Repeat** a season that pays **in full**.
- **Balance.** Field Theory **+4 / +7 / +10**, Basic and Heavy Shield Core **50 / 55 %**, Engine II and III **3 / 4 %**, Adaptive Cores at half, the Afterburner **+20 / 30 / 40 % for 15 s**.
- **Skylab.** Solar keeps **100 %** of its power while it upgrades, and a running upgrade can be **cancelled for a full refund**.
- **Smaller:** no respawn on the spot in a Danger Sector; a cloaked ship cannot use the giant excavator; the Thulium Geode pays **72 to 168** Thulium; Moles can share an asteroid; special items are tiles of the Hangar inventory; the daily gifts are x3 and x4 ammo and tier III rockets, and the calendar is worth **50 %** more.

**If you already play: what changes for you**
- **Update the game.** The server and the new game go live together. The update itself pays, moves and removes no Credits, Thulium or items; what you own takes the new values at once.
- **A 0.4.27 game keeps working** but cannot open or enter a Gate, cannot pick the new ammo, still shows laser lines for aliens and shows old screens in places.
- **x4 ammo:** the Experimental Fusion Core you hold stays yours. To make more, research Military Grade Ammo I and II; a Skylab Ammo Printer set to x3 or x4 makes x2 until you have them.
- **Repeats** open at the first wipe after the update, not before.
- **A Solar upgrade under way** no longer leaves your farms dark. **Daily rewards:** the season that is running keeps its calendar.

**Clan Gates**
- **How a run goes.** On the **Gates** tab a co-leader or the leader picks a stage and presses **Summon**; the price comes out of the clan bank. Clan members press **Enter** while they fly, in a group with at least **4** members of the clan, and the pilot who opened the gate or an officer presses **Start**. A gate nobody starts within **10 minutes** closes and its price goes back to the bank.
- **The limits.** A clan opens at most **3 gates a day** (UTC), one at a time, and a stage only after it has cleared the stage before it that season. A world holds at most **6** open gates, one for each map; when all are in use a clan tries again a few minutes later. You enter with a ship in flight, out of combat, at the stage's pilot level (**6 / 7 / 8**). Inside a gate nobody can attack anyone, the Jump CPU and the Base CPU do not work and you cannot change world; **Leave** takes you out. A pilot who left or was destroyed can fly back in **3 times, 20 seconds apart**.
- **The maze.** One of **8 layouts** on one of 6 maps (Gate Delta, Epsilon, Zeta, Eta, Theta and Iota); walls stop ships and shots, and the minimap draws only the rooms you have explored. Four kinds of alien sleep in the rooms and wake in packs: Gate Goombah, Gate Pirate, Gate Crystalys and Gate Crystalys Twin, **195** in all for a party of 5, at most 10 alive for each pilot and 70 in all. Stage 2 has **1.5 times** the hull and shield of stage 1 and **1.25 times** the damage, stage 3 **2.5 times** and **1.5 times**. The number of aliens is the same at every stage, so stages 2 and 3 take longer.
- **Loot zones.** Each maze has **4**. Stand in one for 2 seconds and a wave of 10 Gate Goombahs and a Gate Crystalys comes for it; keep a pilot inside for **30 seconds** (the hold stops while 3 or more aliens stand in the ring) and the group has 45 seconds to vote for one of three cards. A card is Thulium (2,000 / 3,000 / 5,000), Velkonite or Orvium Reinforced Plates or ore, Ultra Core, Experimental Fusion Core, Dark Matter or a Dark Matter Plate, and now and then (1 % of the cards) a piece of gear for one pilot of the party: Engine III, Heavy Shield Core, Adaptive Core III or Starfire-III. Cards are paid with the Warlord's pay.
- **The Warlord.** A Crystalys three times the size, with **10,000,000 hull and 8,000,000 shield** at stage 1 for a party of 5 (15 and 12 million at stage 2, 25 and 20 million at stage 3), tougher with every pilot in the party. It uses one ability at a time, at random, each with a cooldown of 2 minutes: **Lifesteal aura**, **Meteor drop**, **Focus on healers**, **Rocket barrage** (an EMP Charge or a cloak shakes the rockets off) and **Shield absorption**.
- **Time.** A gate fails and pays nothing after **80 / 110 / 150 minutes** from its start, or when nobody has been inside for 3 minutes. After the Warlord falls the gate stays open for 2 more minutes. Open gates end when the server restarts, and their price goes back to the clan bank.

| Stage | Honor | Experience | Credits | Thulium | x4 ammo | Clan bank, first clear |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 25,000 | 600,000 | 5,000,000 | 4,000 | 4,000 | 10,000,000 |
| 2 | 50,000 | 1,500,000 | 10,000,000 | 9,000 | 9,000 | 20,000,000 |
| 3 | 100,000 | 2,400,000 | 17,500,000 | 15,000 | 15,000 | 30,000,000 |

- **Who is paid.** The aliens pay nothing; the Warlord's fall pays. A stage pays a pilot **once per UTC day**, and a pilot is paid for at most **10 stage clears a week** (Monday to Sunday, UTC). Entry is never refused for that: the clear is played and pays nothing, and the result screen says why. A paid clear writes a line in your Logbook.
- **What it takes.** Be inside at least 2 minutes and have a share in the fight: deal 2 % of the Warlord's hull and shield, or destroy 10 of the gate's aliens, or heal other pilots for 50,000 during the Warlord fight.
- **The same in every world.** There is no world multiplier inside a gate. The experience counts for your PvE ranking points, 1 point for every 1,000 (600 / 1,500 / 2,400 for a stage).
- **The clan bank** gets its Credits the first time the clan clears a stage in a season, if the clan is at least 3 days old and at least 3 pilots of that clear were paid.
- **What a day and a week can bring a pilot:** every stage once in a day pays 175,000 Honor, 4,500,000 experience, 32,500,000 Credits, 28,000 Thulium and 28,000 x4 ammo; the best week (seven stage 3 and three stage 2 clears) pays 850,000 Honor, 21,300,000 experience, 152,500,000 Credits, 132,000 Thulium and 132,000 x4 ammo.

**The Tesseract and the boss swarms**
- **Where and when.** From season day 4 until the wipe. The Phantasm and Goombah swarms live on `x-3` and `x-4` of every company (6 of each in a world), the Crystalys swarm in `DS-1`, `DS-2` and `DS-3` and the Tesseract in `DS-4`. The Danger Sectors are PvP, so a fight there can draw rivals.

| Swarm | Leader, hull / shield in Alpha | Followers | Back after the leader falls |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phantasm | Boss Phantasm 40,000 / 64,000 | up to 4 Phantasm Guards, a new one every 10 s, each mends 30 hull a second | 2 min |
| Goombah | Boss Goombah 128,000 / 192,000 | up to 4 Goombah Guards, a new one every 10 s, each mends 110 hull a second | 5 min |
| Crystalys | Boss Crystalys 448,000 / 280,000 | up to 3 Crystalys Guards, a new one every 10 s, each mends 250 hull a second | 30 min |
| Tesseract | Tesseract 1,600,000 / 1,200,000 | up to 50 Facets, 10 more every 5 s while it is hit | 30 min |

- **What they pay in Alpha** (Beta twice, Gamma three times; the hull, shield and damage are 1.5 and 2 times):

| Leader | Credits | Thulium | Experience | Honor | PvE points |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boss Phantasm | 39,000 | 195 | 7,800 | 62 | 8 |
| Boss Goombah | 120,000 | 600 | 24,000 | 192 | 14 |
| Boss Crystalys | 393,750 | 1,050 | 63,000 | 273 | 21 |
| Tesseract | 900,000 | 2,400 | 144,000 | 624 | 42 |

- **How the pay goes.** The leaders never start a fight: they roam until a pilot hits them, then fight back together with the ships near them. The pay is split by damage among the pilots who did their share, and the box is for the pilot who dealt the most. A Guard is worth 1, 3 or 6 PvE points (Phantasm, Goombah, Crystalys). The Crystalys box holds Ultra Core and Experimental Fusion Core; the Tesseract box plates, Power Cores, Ancient Control Units and now and then Dark Matter.
- **The Tesseract's fight.** It fires nothing and never chases anyone; its defence is its mend and its Facets. Never leave it alone: after 5 seconds without damage it mends its hull and then its shield at 125,000 a second in Alpha (187,500 in Beta, 250,000 in Gamma). Every Facet has **20,000 hull and 16,000 shield** and hits for **556** a volley in Alpha at speed 450, and all of them hunt the pilot with the most damage on the Tesseract, who is changed only when another pilot has clearly overtaken him. A Facet pays nothing and drops nothing. The Facets leave 20 seconds after the last hit and 1 minute after the Tesseract falls.
- **Who they are for.** The Phantasm swarm for a group of mid-level pilots, the Goombah swarm for a group of the strongest ships, the Crystalys swarm for a large group, the Tesseract for a very large one.

**Laser ammo**

| Ammo | Damage | Research | Made from |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ultra Core | x3, pierces 5 % | Military Grade Ammo I, 30 min | still sold for 1 Thulium; can be crafted, 1,000 at a time |
| Experimental Fusion Core | x4, pierces 10 % | Military Grade Ammo II, 4 h | craft only, from raw materials |
| Siphon Battery | x1 on the shield only, you take what it drains | none | now sold for **50 Credits** (0.25 Thulium before) |
| Siphon Battery II | x0.5 on the shield only, you take **twice** what it drains | 1 h | 1,000 Siphon Battery, 250 Thulium |
| Antimatter Battery I | x2, pierces 20 % | 3 h | 1,000 Siphon Battery II, 100 Thulium |
| Antimatter Battery II | x3, pierces 20 % | 8 h | 1,000 Antimatter Battery I, 3 Dark Matter, 4,740 Credits, 75 Thulium |
| Dark Matter Ammo I | x1.5 to x5 for every volley, x3.25 on average | 1 h | 2,000 Ship Fragment, 2,000 Cataclysite, 1 Dark Matter, 4,913 Credits, 800 Thulium |
| Dark Matter Ammo II | x6, one volley every 1.5 s, gives you 25 % of the damage the target's shield took | 6 h | 1,000 Dark Matter Ammo I, 4 Dark Matter, 200 Thulium |

- **Crafts** make 1,000 units in 5 to 15 minutes in the Assembly. The Ultra Core and the Experimental Fusion Core are made from raw materials (the Experimental Fusion Core costs 1,000 Cataclysite, 1,000 Ship Fragment, 100 Power Cores, 1,000 Quorvium, 8 Velkonite Reinforced Plates and 1 Orvium Reinforced Plate, 9,138 Credits and 1,050 Thulium), never from the ammo below it.
- **The Skylab Ammo Printer** makes the Ultra Core and the Experimental Fusion Core once you have researched them; its x2 mode and the Rocket Factory are open to all.
- **A choice, not a step up.** Antimatter opens the hull sooner against ships with a big shield next to a small hull; the x4 hits harder against everything else. One roll of Dark Matter Ammo I serves the whole ship's volley. Dark Matter Ammo II hits for the same damage a second as the x4.
- The five new ammo can be sold on the Auction like the others (89 kinds can be listed now). The Archivist achievement asks for all **158** technologies, the seven Laser Ammo ones among them; a pilot who has the achievement keeps it.

**Repeating missions after a wipe**
- **Which.** The 88 level missions (the 8 Specials among them), the 8 Asteroids missions and all 50 Challenge missions, as far as you have completed them. Station missions cannot be repeated.
- **When.** After a wipe every completed mission is open for **one Repeat per mission and season**; Mission Control marks it "Repeat: full rewards". A mission you completed or repeated since the last wipe stays closed until the next. It plays like the mission: the same steps, time limit and conditions, one of your 5 slots (one of the 3 places of the Challenge line for a Challenge).
- **What it pays.** Everything the mission pays: experience, honor, Credits, Thulium, items and booster time, with your world's bonus, your boosters, Premium experience and your clan's boosts. At base, before the world and the boosts, the 88 level missions and 8 Asteroids missions pay **6,869,000 Credits and 52,585 Thulium** together and the 50 Challenge missions **428,325,000 Credits and 2,847,085 Thulium**: **435,194,000 Credits and 2,899,670 Thulium** for a pilot who repeats them all. The items of a Repeat cannot be sold on the Auction.
- **Wipe Points.** A Repeat of a level mission counts like a first completion, once per mission and season, up to the 100th mission: the missions' Wipe Points now reach **105**, and a pilot who has all 88 gains 15 more by repeating them. The sources of Wipe Points pay up to 1,105 a wipe (1,090 before). Repeats of Asteroids and Challenge missions do not count.
- **What it does not do.** A Repeat counts for no achievement or title, the Stats page or the Logbook, and unlocks nothing. If you fail it or abandon it, the mission is open for a Repeat again. A finished Repeat that is not claimed when the wipe comes stays claimable and pays in full; one still running is dropped.

**Aliens' shots and sounds**
- **Six shapes.** Seekers, Phantasms and Davidski fire glowing plasma blobs, Goombahs sticky lime spores, Crystalys tumbling crystal shards, Pirates red slugs with a trail of smoke, the Dormant, the Slumbering Voids, the Facets and the aliens of the lost civilisation violet ion orbs, and Bulwarks and the Clan Wardens heavy lumps of bronze-rimmed steel. A boss's shot is **1.6 times** bigger and **1.4 times** brighter. An alien the game does not know fires plasma.
- **32 new sounds.** A shot sound and an impact sound for every family, in several variants, and a heavier pair for the bosses, in place of the alien warble.
- **As instant as a laser.** The damage number appears with the shot as before. Your lasers, the lasers of company pilots, the Dormant Swamp's turrets and every rocket are as they were.

**Balance**

| | 0.4.27 | 0.5.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Field Theory I / II / III (the total at that level) | +2 / +3 / +5 points of shield absorption | **+4 / +7 / +10** |
| Basic / Heavy Shield Core absorbance (Light stays 45 %) | 48 / 50 % | **50 / 55 %** |
| Engine II / III speed bonus (Engine I stays 2 %) | 4 / 5 % | **3 / 4 %** |
| Adaptive Core I / II / III speed bonus | 2.4 / 3.2 / 4 % | **1.2 / 1.6 / 2 %** |
| Afterburner I / II / III | +30 / 45 / 60 % for 10 s | **+20 / 30 / 40 % for 15 s** |

- **Shields.** The best shield out of the box (a Heavy Shield Core with three Absorption Shield Cell IV) is now **85 %** (80 %). Absorbance is not capped at 100 %, so the most a pilot can reach rises with it.
- **Speed.** Everything with an Engine or an Adaptive Core is slower: the fastest Wraith build goes from about 850 to about 786, the fastest Ironclad build from about 820 to about 751. Several engines make the Afterburner last longer: 15 s, 22.5 s with two and 30 s with three; the cooldowns are the same. The Skylab's engines are a little slower too (a station with five fully fitted Engine IIIs needs 33 minutes for a hop, it needed 32).
- **What follows.** Davidski's gear gives him 86.3 % absorbance (80.5 %) and speed 89 (96). The Slumbering Void is now faster than a Storm on Afterburner III. Nothing can leave the black hole from within about **440** units (about 390 before), and a ship has to press the Afterburner earlier to be saved from its pull; the black hole itself did not change. A lone level 8 Paragon now just beats the Pirate Boss on `x-3` in Alpha with x2 ammo (calculated: 4 % of its hull left at the lowest) and two win safely; in Beta and Gamma a lone Paragon is destroyed.

**Skylab**
- **Solar at 100 %.** While Solar upgrades it keeps making all the power of its current level, and the new level's power takes over when the upgrade ends. A Solar upgrade never stops your farms and collectors, never leaves the station in deficit and never keeps the Forgery from starting a batch. A Solar upgrade under way when the server updates no longer leaves your farms dark: they work again from the server's start, and the dark time is not paid back. The briefings of the Station missions say so.
- **Cancel an upgrade.** The card of a running upgrade has a **Cancel upgrade** button. After you confirm, you get back **everything the start took**: the Credits, the Thulium and the Dark Matter Plates, as you paid them even if prices have changed. Only the time is lost. The module goes back as it was, with the same level and switch and what it had stored. An upgrade that has already finished cannot be cancelled. One that is under way when the server updates can be cancelled too, and is refunded at the price of its level.
- **Ammo Printer.** The x3 and x4 modes need Military Grade Ammo I and II (see Laser ammo).
- **Survey Canister.** Its four Common stacks are smaller: Reinforced Hull Plates **100** (1,300), Ship Fragments **1,000** (9,000), Power Cores **20** (450) and Regular Cluster Chunks **2** (4). No chance of any prize changed.

**Clan Wardens**
- **A mix in every wave.** A wave used to be one kind of alien. Now it is a mix of Phantasm, Bulwarks and Goombahs on every map, as many aliens as before. The Wardens II and III, the Wrath Warden III apart, call 3 Phantasm, 1 Bulwark and 1 Goombah on `x-2` and 5, 3 and 2 on `x-3` and `x-4`; the Wrath Warden III 4, 2 and 2 on `x-2` and 7, 4 and 4 on `x-3` and `x-4`.
- **The Recruit Wardens call no Goombah.** The three Wardens I call 4 Phantasm and 1 Bulwark on `x-2` and 8 Phantasm and 2 Bulwarks on `x-3` and `x-4`.
- **Crews (calculated, Alpha, x2 ammo).** The smallest crew that wins against the Brood, Siege and Wrath Warden I goes on `x-4` from 69, 56 and 62 pilots to **47, 43 and 48**, so those maps get easier, and on `x-2` and `x-3` it asks 1 to 3 more pilots than before. The Wardens II and III ask up to 8 more pilots on `x-2` and `x-3`. In Gamma `x-3`, where the aliens of a wave are twice as strong, the Siege Warden I now asks **56** pilots (44 before) and the Wrath Warden I **62** (49), more than the 50 members of a level 3 clan.
- **Pay and notices.** A wave pays more: 29,000 / 60,000 / 60,000 Credits in Alpha for a Warden II (15,000 / 30,000 / 50,000 before), 17,000 / 34,000 / 34,000 for a Warden I. The clan is told one line for each kind in a wave. Bulwarks and Goombahs on `x-2` and Phantasm on `x-4`, which those maps do not have of their own, leave 5 minutes after the Warden unless pilots are still fighting them.

**Danger Sectors and the giant excavator**
- **No respawn on the spot in a Danger Sector.** If you are destroyed in `DS-1` to `DS-4`, in any world, the death screen offers your **base** and the **nearest portal**, and "On the spot" is greyed out with the reason. A request for it is refused and costs nothing.
- **A cloaked ship cannot use the giant excavator.** The sheet's buttons are shut and every action is refused until the cloak ends. A cloaked ship may still pick up its boxes.
- **Whose run it is.** The excavator's sheet and its start message show who started the run and the Excavator Mining share its boxes carry. A pilot who owns Excavator Mining is told that it counts on the runs he starts himself. A research that finishes while you fly counts at your next Start.

**Daily rewards**
- **Ammo and rockets only.** A daily gift is one of six: Ultra Core, Experimental Fusion Core, Lancet III, Rivet III, Ember III or Scatter III. A full calendar is worth about 50 % more than before. The chests at 7, 14, 21 and 28 days and the Season prize are not daily gifts and stay as they are. The wipe carries ammo and rockets over, up to 1,000 of each rocket and 1,000,000 of each ammo type.
- **When.** The season that is running keeps its calendar; the calendars drawn from now on hold the new gifts.

**Smaller changes**
- **Thulium Geode:** **72 to 168** Thulium (36 to 84 before); its Credits are the same.
- **Moles:** the Moles of one pilot take the nearest asteroid each, so five Moles with one asteroid in reach all work it and break it sooner; their beams lie side by side. Pulses that arrive after the one that breaks an asteroid are lost.
- **Repair slots:** switching on the Repair Drone of an extra slot (REP) plays a soft repair pulse and floats the hull it heals each second over your ship, as the Emergency Repair does. The Auto-Repair CPU and the repair ships at the company bases are unchanged.
- **Hangar page:** the Containers button is gone from the inventory (the Containers page stays), each special item you hold is a tile among the consumables, and the grey hint line under the grid is gone.
- **Bonus codes** can give special items beside their other rewards.
- **Away mode is off.** A window you have left (alt-tabbed or minimised) is sent the full stream, as the open one is, so the world is not old when you come back.
- **Pirate Boss:** its box holds 1,000 to 2,000 of Advanced Plasma, Siphon Battery or Siphon Battery II (one of the three, picked at random), and is worth a little under half of what the kill pays.
- **Wiki:** new pages for the Gates and for the Phantasm, Goombah, Crystalys and Tesseract swarms, and the pages the changes above touch follow them, in 13 languages.

**A 0.4.27 game on the 0.5.0 server**
- It keeps working and loses no pay, but it cannot open or enter a Gate (it is told to update) and it shows old screens in places: aliens fire laser lines, the Tesseract looks like a big Crystalys and the Facets like Seekers, the beams of all but one of the Moles at a shared asteroid go quiet, the ammo picker is a fixed list of the five old ammo (the new ones are plain items it cannot pick), the death panel of a Danger Sector says "The place where you died is not known" next to the greyed "On the spot", the excavator's start message reads in English, and an open Repeat is not shown.

**For administrators and the server**
- **Dungeons tab:** the admin page has a tab (English) for the Gates: a kill switch, every open run with its pilots, and an eject, a teleport, an end and a force-clear, each with a confirmation and an audit record. A pilot can be taken out of a gate whatever its state, logged on or off.
- **Set season day, backwards:** a set-back now pays the clans' daily bonus again for the replayed days (from the clans' banks; nothing is taken back) and reopens the login calendar's collected day tiles of those days, which pay their gift again. A forward set, the same day twice and a Reset change nothing.
- **Login calendar drafts:** a draft that was made from the old gifts and not approved is drawn again from the new ones by the server. An approved draft keeps its gifts until an administrator re-rolls it.
